title: The Crooked Veil Again
premise: Orsen Delacroix, a mercenary bound to a silent god and hiding in the Veil—a valley where magic cannot enter—has spent ten years burying the past. When a child named Sable arrives speaking the dead tongue of the first kingdoms, Orsen learns she is the last vessel of their god's voice, hunted by the Hollow King, a monarch consumed by the entity wearing his crown. To save her, Orsen must leave the valley that kept them safe and unbind the king before the entity finishes devouring him and turns its hunger on the world. In the end, Orsen breaks their oath to the god to free both king and child, discovering that belonging was never granted by divine contract but chosen in the act of sacrifice—and they return to the valley not as a fugitive, but as Sable's guardian.
about_author: Yara Yarrow is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval oaths and liturgical fragments before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about broken promises, found family, and the gods we outgrow.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Ten years after fleeing into the magic-dead valley of Greyhollow, Orsen tends goats and drinks away memories of the god Veyl who went silent mid-oath. A storm brings a knock at the door: a mud-caked child, perhaps eight years old, speaking a language Orsen recognizes from forbidden prayers. Emotional beat: dread cracking open long-buried purpose.

chapters.title: A Tongue Older Than Crowns
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. The child, Sable, cannot speak any living language, but her words make old scars ache and dead wards hum. Orsen realizes she carries a fragment of Veyl's voice—the god didn't die, it was devoured. Riders appear on the ridge bearing the Hollow King's sigil. Emotional beat: reluctant protectiveness hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: What the Oath Still Owes
chapters.summary: Sable's POV, rendered through dreamlike fragments she half-understands. She remembers being a temple orphan, the night the priests sold her voice to the crown, and the thing with too many teeth that wears the king like a coat. She trusts Orsen because the god inside her does. Emotional beat: terror tempered by instinctive trust.

chapters.title: The Price of Staying
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Hollow King soldiers burn the valley's outer farms searching for the child. Orsen's neighbor Maren dies covering their escape, and Orsen learns invisibility was always borrowed time—the entity has been hunting Veyl's vessels for a decade. Emotional beat: guilt transmuted into the decision to finally leave.

chapters.title: Crossing the Veil
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Stepping beyond the valley's border, magic floods back—Orsen's dormant oath-marks ignite, and Sable's fragment of Veyl whispers its first clear word in ten years: 'run.' They evade a checkpoint with help from a disgraced hedge-priest, Brother Callow, who joins them. Emotional beat: vertigo and exhilaration of returning to a hostile world.

chapters.title: The God That Went Quiet
chapters.summary: Callow's POV. At a ruined shrine, Callow reveals what he knows: Veyl wasn't silent by choice—it was eaten piece by piece by an older hunger, the Crownless, which now sits on the throne wearing King Aldric. Each vessel Sable's age has been harvested; she may be the last. Emotional beat: despair confronted honestly, faith questioned without breaking.

chapters.title: Court of Teeth
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Disguised as mercenaries, they infiltrate the capital during the Feast of Unbinding. Orsen sees King Aldric up close: ninety percent gone, eyes like drowned lanterns, briefly surfacing to mouth the words 'kill me' before the Crownless notices and smiles through his face. Emotional beat: horror laced with unexpected pity for the man behind the monster.

chapters.title: The Unbinding Rite
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Captured and brought before the throne, Sable is meant to be the final harvest. But in the throne room, her fragment of Veyl resonates with the shredded remains still trapped inside Aldric, and she begins the unbinding rite from within the enemy's own hall. Emotional beat: small courage becoming enormous.

chapters.title: Where the Hunger Ends
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Climax. Orsen fights through the Crownless's hollowed court to reach the dais, where the rite demands a price: an oath freely broken. Orsen renounces Veyl entirely, pouring ten years of binding into severing the Crownless from Aldric. The god-fragment and the hunger annihilate each other; Aldric collapses, mortal and weeping. Emotional beat: sacrifice as liberation, not loss.

chapters.title: Home Is a Door Left Open
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV, epilogue-like. Aldric, restored but broken, begins repairing a kingdom that barely remembers how to be ruled. Sable, her voice now wholly her own, chooses Orsen over the rebuilt temples. They return to Greyhollow together, where the valley's silence feels less like hiding and more like peace. Emotional beat: quiet, earned belonging.
